cards.name: Dismantle the Device
cards.displayText: Defeat the active Relic.

text.summary: Answers whichever Relic is on the table.
notes: "The active Relic" is a well-defined phrase because a player controls at most one (ruleset update §12). It needs no target primitive of its own: a battlefield selector filtered to relics *is* the active relic, and building a second way to say the same thing would give the rule two places to drift.

`controller` is stated explicitly rather than left to the default, because §12 requires an effect that could reach either player's Relic to say so. `any` is the literal reading of the unqualified card text, so the caster chooses — including, legally, their own.
The spell cannot be played at all when no Relic is in play: the target is required, and the engine refuses a spell with no legal target.

precons.name: Containment Control
precons.strategy: Survive the early game with blockers and disruption, preserve Energy for Reactions, then win through card advantage and Bound Anomaly.

deckPlans.name: Bastion Guardians plan
deckPlans.summary: Block profitably, keep the Units that survive doing it, and turn the formation the opponent failed to break into the attack that wins.

packages.label: Shield wall
packages.rationale: The authored Defenders. They are the resource every other package in this deck spends: a payoff that counts surviving blockers needs blockers that survive.

packages.label: Combat protection
packages.rationale: Reactions that make a block survivable. They only read as good play alongside the wall, and alone they are four cards that do nothing on their own turn.

packages.label: Formation engine
packages.rationale: The Formation, Protection and Defensive Engine cards. Each one raises what the wall is worth rather than adding to it, which is the archetype's whole loop.

packages.label: Counterattack payoff
packages.rationale: The cards that convert a surviving formation into damage. Without them the deck defends indefinitely and never closes, which is the failure mode this package exists against.

packages.label: Guard tokens
packages.rationale: Bodies on demand to fill gaps in the wall. Substitutable, so not core: any cheap Unit does most of this job.

packages.label: Selection
packages.rationale: A defensive deck loses to the one card it did not draw; these are what let it find the missing half of the loop.

deckPlans.name: Containment Control plan
deckPlans.summary: Survive the opening on cheap blockers, answer only what has to be answered, hold Energy open for Reactions, and win late on accumulated cards.

packages.label: Reaction suite
packages.rationale: The cards that require a turn to be spent doing nothing. Their value is entirely in being held, which no per-turn valuation can express and which is why the plan names them as a group.

packages.label: Containment removal
packages.rationale: Proactive answers, spread across Exhaustion, bounce, lockdown and a sweeper so the deck is not narrow against any one board.

packages.label: Reaction engine
packages.rationale: The Reaction Engine, Exhaustion Engine and Tempo cards: they make holding Energy cheaper rather than adding to the board, which is the only way this archetype gains tempo.

packages.label: Early blockers
packages.rationale: Cheap Defenders that hold the board while Energy is being kept open. Losing them is how a reactive deck dies before its answers matter.

packages.label: Card advantage
packages.rationale: Filtering, selection and draw. A deck that answers one threat per turn only wins by having more cards than there are threats, so this is the win condition as much as the finisher is.

packages.label: Late finish
packages.rationale: Two expensive cards the deck is trying to reach. Not core: the archetype is defined by surviving, and a search may find a different way to close.

deckPlans.name: Goblin Swarm plan
deckPlans.summary: Make more Goblins than the opponent can answer one at a time, multiply them, and cash the width in with effects that count Units.

packages.label: Token engine
packages.rationale: Every card here is authored as a Swarm Generator: without them the deck has no board to be wide with, and no other package produces bodies from nothing.

packages.label: Tribal multipliers
packages.rationale: The Multiplier and Tribal Engine cards are worth nothing on an empty board and are the difference between a wide board and a winning one, so they belong with the engine rather than with the payoff.

packages.label: Width payoff
packages.rationale: Each of these scales on how many Units are already out. Held without the engine they are blank; that dependence is exactly what a plan exists to record.

packages.label: Early curve
packages.rationale: Plain one- and two-cost bodies. Interchangeable by design, which is why this package is not core: a search may replace any of them without changing what the deck is.

packages.label: Reach and removal
packages.rationale: The deck's only answers to a blocker it cannot attack past. Not core: the archetype survives losing them, and the search should be free to try that.

deckPlans.name: Grave Sacrifice plan
deckPlans.summary: Keep a supply of expendable Units, keep an outlet to spend them through, and be paid every time one of them is defeated.

packages.label: Sacrifice outlets
packages.rationale: The only cards that turn a Unit into a defeat on demand. Every payoff in this deck is dead without one, and holding three is the reason the deck can rely on them.

packages.label: Fodder supply
packages.rationale: The other half of the outlet: Units and Tokens whose purpose is to be spent. Authored as Fodder, Fodder Generator or Recurring Fodder, so this membership is read off the cards rather than assigned.

packages.label: Death payoff
packages.rationale: What the outlet is for. Each of these reads a defeat and converts it; between them they cover drain, Tokens, damage and a finisher, so the package is what makes the loop worth running.

packages.label: Graveyard recursion
packages.rationale: Fodder that comes back is fodder spent twice. This is what stops the engine from running out, which is the archetype's real limiting resource.

packages.label: Sacrifice removal
packages.rationale: Removal that is paid for with the deck's own fodder, so interaction and engine are the same expenditure. Not core: the archetype still functions with different answers.

packages.label: Attrition draw
packages.rationale: Cards that pay Health or a Unit for cards. Substitutable, so not core, but this is where the deck's card advantage comes from once the board trade stalls.
